title: How property classification works
content: GeoIntel classifies a location as Commercial, Residential, Industrial, Institutional, Landmark, Transport, Mixed Use or Unknown, using only OpenStreetMap features read live from Overpass within the selected radius. It never guesses from the address text or from an AI model's memory. If a building or business is mapped at the point itself (within about 35 metres), that feature is what the classification describes: a house inside a business district is still a house. Street furniture such as benches, bins, parking spaces, toilets, bus stops and information boards cannot be the subject; they only count as evidence about the surrounding area. With a subject, confidence starts at 70% and rises towards 95% the more the surrounding area agrees with it, staying nearer 70-80% where the area points another way. With no subject, the answer describes the surrounding area instead: features nearer the point count for more than distant ones, the top-scoring use wins, the result is Mixed Use when the top two are within 25% of each other, and confidence is capped at 60% however much evidence there is. When nothing is mapped, or nothing mapped carries a specific enough tag to classify, the result is Unknown with no confidence figure. Unknown means not enough mapped detail, never that the place is vacant. OpenStreetMap tags describe how a place is mapped. They are not legal zoning, ownership, value or occupancy, and the classification says nothing about any of those.

title: What VERIFIED, INFERRED, and UNAVAILABLE mean
content: Every property classification in GeoIntel carries a trust level so an estimate is never mistaken for a fact. VERIFIED means a named building or business is mapped at the point itself, so the classification reads that feature's own OpenStreetMap tag. INFERRED means nothing is mapped at the exact point, so the classification is a reading of the surrounding area, which is a reasonable estimate and not a confirmed fact about the building. UNAVAILABLE means there was not enough mapped evidence to classify at all, or the data provider could not be reached. In both cases GeoIntel says so plainly and shows no confidence figure rather than inventing a plausible answer.

title: How GIS evidence and analysis radius work
content: GIS Evidence comes from live Overpass API queries against OpenStreetMap data, run fresh (with caching for a few minutes to reduce load) for the exact coordinates and radius selected. Available radii are 100m, 250m, 500m, 1km, 2km, and 5km, or a custom value up to 5km. The query pulls buildings, shops, offices, amenities, land-use polygons, and points of interest inside that circle, then classifies each one into layers (buildings, shops, offices, amenities, hospitals, schools, restaurants, hotels, parks, water, railways, transport, and more). Roads and administrative boundaries are shown in the layer list but marked 'coming soon' rather than faked, because fetching their full polygon/line geometry responsibly needs a different, tiled fetch strategy than a single Overpass call.

title: How weather and forecast data is sourced
content: Weather data comes from Open-Meteo, a free, keyless weather API, queried live for the selected location's coordinates. GeoIntel shows current temperature, feels-like temperature, condition (translated from Open-Meteo's numeric WMO weather codes into plain text like 'Mainly clear' or 'Light rain'), humidity, wind speed, precipitation, sunrise/sunset times, and a multi-day forecast. If Open-Meteo can't be reached, the Weather panel shows a 'temporarily unavailable' state rather than a stale or fabricated forecast.

title: How routing, directions, and ride booking work
content: Turn-by-turn routes are calculated live by OSRM (Open Source Routing Machine) public routers, with car, walking, and bicycle modes, each using a dedicated router profile. GeoIntel shows distance, estimated duration, and how many alternative routes exist. The 'book a ride' links (Uber, Rapido, Ola, Google Maps) open the provider's own app or website with the route prefilled where that provider supports it - GeoIntel does not process bookings, payments, or show live fares itself, because no free service provides real fare/availability data without a paid partnership. This is the same honest, no-fake-data approach used everywhere else in the product.

title: How Nearby search works
content: The Nearby panel searches OpenStreetMap via Overpass for real points of interest around the selected location across 13 categories: restaurants, cafes, hotels, hospitals, schools, ATMs, banks, petrol stations, shopping, parks, pharmacies, police, and public transport. Results are sorted by straight-line distance from the selected point and capped at the closest 60 (60 shown per category page). Every result includes its OpenStreetMap source tags for transparency.

title: What the AI Copilot and AI Agents can and cannot do
content: The GeoIntel AI Copilot and the six intelligence agents (Search, GIS, Property, Navigation, Travel, and Make My Trip) only ever reason over data that is already real and already on screen for the currently selected location - the live GIS evidence, property classification, weather, nearby results, and route data described in this knowledge base - plus these knowledge-base articles about how the product itself works. They do not have access to the live internet beyond that, do not know about locations other than the one currently selected, and are instructed to say plainly when they don't have enough information rather than inventing an answer. If the AI provider is temporarily unreachable, the Copilot and agents show a clear 'AI temporarily unavailable' message instead of a wrong or fabricated answer.
